stories.title: A guide to qualitative research methods
stories.summary: This overview covers usability testing, user interviews, field studies, and diary studies. The article estimates the cost and difficulty of each method, noting that these figures are rough and relative. Your final costs will depend on your participants, your tools, and how you adapt the method to your needs.

stories.title: AI struggles to design from raw data
stories.summary: Researchers tested whether AI could generate interfaces from raw user data versus synthesized findings. The model produced better designs when provided with pre-processed recommendations rather than raw comments. Teams currently deciding how to integrate AI into design workflows may find that the machine still requires human synthesis.

stories.summary: Why a game? I spend most of my days trying to make software effortless. Information should be easy to find, interfaces should be obvious, and nobody should have to fight to get what they came for. We’re getting pretty good at this. Information is practically free, AI is making it

stories.title: In making things, we make ourselves
stories.summary: Reflections from the Toyota museum in Nagoya, Japan. My family and I recently spent a morning at the Toyota Commemorative Museum of Industry and Technology. Interestingly, Toyota didn’t start with cars , its origins were in textile machinery, with Sakichi Toyoda’s inventions in automatic weaving. His son Kiichiro later brought

stories.title: University platform usability falls short
stories.summary: A study of 304 students in the Russian Federation found that university digital platforms averaged 62.40 on the System Usability Scale. This score sits below the industry benchmark of 68, placing the platforms in the borderline category between marginal and acceptable. The portal has not commented.

stories.title: Cardiometabolic app faces usability hurdles
stories.summary: A mobile health platform for older patients managing cardiometabolic conditions showed marginal usability and significant learning hurdles during testing in Xinjiang, China. The study evaluated the tool among patients with multiple coexisting diseases. The transition from hospital to home remains a complex environment for digital health tools.

stories.title: Digital decision aid for IBD shows promise
stories.summary: A web-based decision aid, I(BD) SELECT, demonstrated good usability during alpha testing with patients and clinicians in Belgium. The tool is designed to support preference-sensitive treatment choices for inflammatory bowel disease. The study highlights the role of digital aids in navigating complex long-term disease management options.

stories.title: Meet the innovators exhibiting at Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026
stories.summary: In our photo essay from BTS at the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre, we showcase highlights from the exhibition halls. Launched in 2014, PhotoSparks is a weekly feature from YourStory, with photographs that celebrate the spirit of creativity and innovation. In the earlier 1,030 posts, we featured an art festival, cartoon

stories.summary: Artificial Intelligence - Interaction - Management - Research Pass at least 5 courses in one topic, and receive Specialty recognition on your UX Certificate. A specialty is not required to earn a UX Certificate. Live online courses about UX best practices, proven methods, and hands-on exercises led by NN/g experts

stories.title: Allo typeface offers Inter with a warmer character
stories.summary: Josh Puckett has released Allo, an open-source variable typeface based on Inter 4.1. The font includes three variable axes, 606 glyphs, and true italics drawn from scratch. Every glyph was redrawn to provide a warmer character for digital design projects. The typeface is available free of charge.

stories.title: Klim Type Foundry releases Die Grotesk on GitHub
stories.summary: Klim Type Foundry has introduced Die Grotesk, its first public variable font hosted on GitHub. The typeface features an optical size axis that adjusts spacing between 6 and 42 points automatically. The foundry used Haas metal specimens to inform the design, aiming to recover the texture of small text.

stories.title: Ukraine introduces national font to replace Russian types
stories.summary: Ukraine has unveiled a new national font called Zakon, meaning law, to replace Russian-designed typefaces on official documents. The Ministry of Culture stated that the country will phase out fonts like Izhitsa, which are produced by the Russian foundry ParaType. Official documents will now be set in Zakon.

stories.title: Mutabor Unveils the Voith brand identity
stories.summary: Mutabor builds the Voith brand identity around movement: a V-Vector symbol, a custom typeface, and a blue made for screens. The whole system starts with a single chevron. Mutabor calls it the V-Vector, a > that points forward and never sits still: it repeats into a pattern on the Appleton

stories.title: Branding: Zero 10 brand identity by Saffron
stories.summary: Saffron builds the Zero 10 brand identity for Art Basel from Malevich's 1915 0,10 show, a frame-like mark for digital art. The mark itself does almost nothing, and that is the point. Two numerals, a round zero and a straight ten, sit far apart, open space held between them. The

stories.title: How&Howâs Rebellious Packaging Design for Wild Thingz
stories.summary: How&Howâs packaging design for plant-based candy Wild Thingz pairs dark pouches with Venus flytrap mascot Vee to disrupt UK sweet aisles. A bright green supermarket basket sits on cracked grey concrete, stuffed with dark pouches while weeds push straight through the pavement beside it. That opening frame sets the tone

stories.title: Werklig designs Voltcore identity
stories.summary: Helsinki studio Werklig designed the web identity for Finnish energy firm Voltcore. The site features a minimalist layout with a spaced wordmark and monospaced links, set against imagery of foggy snow ridges. The company develops grid-balancing, baseload, and hybrid power assets across the Nordic region.

stories.title: Smith & Diction updates PHS brand
stories.summary: Smith & Diction redesigned the Pennsylvania Horticultural Society brand identity, replacing a circular tree logo with a plant-based mark. The new design incorporates three plants growing from the PHS letters. The organization manages gardens, parks, and the Philadelphia Flower Show across the region.

stories.title: OMSE creates B416 identity
stories.summary: London studio OMSE developed a visual identity for the Before 16 campaign, which advocates for raising the social media age limit in New Zealand. The B416 mark mimics film age ratings, using a compact, stamp-like design intended to accommodate new tiers as the campaign expands its scope.

stories.title: Ava Roth collaborates with bees
stories.summary: Artist Ava Roth uses honeybees to complete her Kintsu-Bee series, which involves placing broken ceramics into hives. The bees form honeycombs that bond the fractured pieces, a process inspired by the Japanese kintsugi technique of repairing pottery with gold. The bees provide the structural adhesive.

stories.title: British Rail design manual from 1965
stories.summary: The 1965 British Rail design manual, created by the Design Research Unit, established a unified visual identity for the state-run rail service. It introduced the Rail Alphabet typeface to replace Gill Sans and standardized colour schemes for all rolling stock to improve cohesion across the network.

stories.title: Wiedemann Lampe creates verbal-led identity for Haringey’s 2027 Borough of Culture year - Design Week
Figma adds agent to workflow
stories.summary: Figma has introduced a workflow tool featuring Specs and the Figma agent to centralize diagrams, designs, and technical decisions. The platform provides a container for project context, allowing teams to compare prototypes and collaborate on implementation directly within the canvas. The agent assists in managing these project assets.

stories.title: How I Used AI to Make My Grandson a Children’s Book for Less Than $200 - WSJ
OpenAI tightens model reasoning security
stories.summary: OpenAI has implemented new safeguards to prevent the extraction of internal reasoning from its GPT-6.2 models. The company reports that successful attacks on protected reasoning dropped from 54 percent to 0.2 percent in internal tests. The defenses include targeted training, input filters, and API blocks.

stories.title: Canva now lets you opt out of AI features and I hope every other app follows suit - Stuff
Canva adds generative AI controls
stories.summary: Canva now allows Free and Pro users to disable generative AI tools and reduce the visibility of AI-made assets in its content library. These settings provide individual users with control over their workspace, a feature previously restricted to administrators managing organizational accounts. The controls carry no extra charge.

stories.title: Anthropic mathematician claims Riemann Hypothesis solution
stories.summary: Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, has announced a claimed solution to the 167-year-old Riemann Hypothesis. The problem, which concerns the distribution of prime numbers, is one of the Millennium Prize math problems. If the result is verified, it would represent a significant development in mathematics.

stories.title: Google Gemini adds background Mac automation
stories.summary: Google has introduced a Computer Use feature for its Gemini Mac app, allowing the AI to perform multistep tasks in the background. Users can prompt the model to navigate menus, click, and type across local apps. The process runs in an isolated window, leaving the main cursor free.

stories.title: Canva offers AI feature toggle
stories.summary: Canva has introduced an option for users to disable its generative AI tools. The update follows a broader industry trend of providing users with more control over AI integrations within their software. The platform remains a graphic design tool, now with fewer active generative features for those opting out.

stories.title: Nvidia nears Inception acquisition
stories.summary: Nvidia is reportedly in talks to acquire AI startup Inception for at least $500 million. The startup develops language models using diffusion processes, which refine responses step by step rather than token by token. The deal includes performance bonuses for the company's staff of over 30 employees.

stories.title: Adobe Premiere AI editing workflow
stories.summary: Adobe Premiere users can now edit video by deleting words from AI-generated transcripts. The software also includes tools for audio enhancement, auto-ducking, and generative clip lengthening. These features are licensed for commercial use and allow for automated reframing of footage into vertical or square formats.

stories.title: Hermes Agent adds skill sharing
stories.summary: Nous Research is bringing its open-source Hermes Agent to Microsoft Teams, allowing users to delegate tasks like financial analysis and document drafting. A new Collective Wisdom feature enables employees to share successful automated workflows as reusable skills across their teams. The agents run in isolated microVMs.

stories.title: Signal to restrict screenshots
stories.summary: Signal plans to restrict the screenshot function on mobile devices to prevent AI agents from accessing private conversations. The messaging service has called on Apple, Google, and Microsoft to provide better tools for blocking OS-level data access. Signal admits the current measure is not a complete solution.

stories.title: Onlook launches as an open-source design tool
stories.summary: Onlook is an open-source, AI-first design tool that allows users to visually build, style, and edit code on a canvas. It works with live app code from Git repositories and supports third-party AI agents. The platform is positioned as an open-source alternative to Figma and V0.

stories.title: Webflow adds custom code API for script management
stories.summary: Webflow's Data API allows users to register tracking scripts and apply them to specific landing pages. Because the endpoint replaces existing scripts upon each request, the company recommends a read-merge-write function to prevent accidental deletion of previous code. The process requires a manual publish to finalize changes.

stories.title: Webflow updates CMS API for programmatic content
stories.summary: Webflow's CMS API now allows users to write and publish content directly into collections from their own code. The platform supports one-off edits via an AI agent or scheduled synchronization through the Webflow JavaScript SDK. This removes the need to manually retype marketing content into the editor.

stories.title: Webflow feed widget automates Instagram content
stories.summary: Webflow users can now embed Instagram feeds using third-party widgets like Elfsight to avoid manual double-posting. The setup requires pasting embed code into a Site plan element. Meta shut down the Instagram Basic Display API on December 4, 2024, affecting how some tools connect to the platform.

stories.title: Webflow integrates Cookiebot for GDPR compliance
stories.summary: Webflow sites can now use Cookiebot to block analytics and ad cookies until visitors provide consent. The integration uses an auto-blocking script in the site head to manage Google Consent Mode v2. This allows campaign measurement to continue functioning after a visitor makes a selection.

stories.title: Webflow adds native HubSpot form integration
stories.summary: Webflow's native HubSpot app allows users to route form submissions into a CRM without rebuilding designs in the HubSpot editor. The app uses a capture script to read form fields upon submission. The integration maintains original site styling, though some limitations apply to specific field types.

stories.title: Webflow introduces native modal scroll locking
stories.summary: Webflow's native Modal element now includes a checkbox to lock page scrolling while a modal is open. Older div-based modals built with Interactions require custom jQuery scripts or attributes to achieve the same effect. Some older versions of iOS ignore the standard overflow hidden CSS property.

stories.title: Webflow updates form notification settings
stories.summary: Webflow now allows users to configure unique notification recipients and reply-to addresses for every form on a site. Since October 2025, each form's settings panel includes five fields to customize email alerts. The subject line remains restricted to the site and form names.

stories.title: Webflow adds Booking.com affiliate widget support
stories.summary: Webflow users can embed Booking.com affiliate widgets to display hotel search and maps directly on their pages. The generated code requires specific data attributes to ensure the widget scales correctly on mobile devices. A height setting of 100 percent can cause the script to overflow its container.

stories.title: Figma AI adds multi-model image comparison
stories.summary: Figma has updated its AI tools to allow users to generate and compare multiple images on a single canvas. Users can view results from up to three different models simultaneously using the same prompt. The update includes support for GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst and NanoBanana models.

stories.title: Gestalt AI outperforms Claude Fable in design benchmark
stories.summary: A stealth AI model called Gestalt was preferred by professional designers in 78 percent of blind head-to-head votes against Claude Fable 5.2. As of November 19, 2026, Gestalt held a 1,931 Elo rating on the Frontier Design Benchmark. The human reference work remains higher than Fable.

stories.title: India highlights digital accessibility initiatives
stories.summary: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology met with the UN Special Rapporteur on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities to discuss digital inclusion. The ministry showcased the GIGW 3.0 guidelines and the IS 17802 standard for ICT accessibility, which are now enforceable under amended national legislation.

stories.title: Govt showcases India
stories.summary: Govt showcases India's digital accessibility initiatives to UN disability rights expert New Delhi: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) held discussions with United Nations Special Rapporteur on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Heba Hagrass highlighting India's efforts to advance digital accessibility and inclusion for persons with disabilities,

stories.title: MeitY outlines digital accessibility framework
stories.summary: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology discussed India's legal framework for digital accessibility with the UN Special Rapporteur. The session highlighted the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act of 2016 and the GIGW 3.0 guidelines, which aim to make government websites and digital services more accessible.

stories.title: MeitY hosts UN Special Rapporteur on digital inclusion
stories.summary: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology held an interactive session with UN Special Rapporteur Heba Hagrass to discuss digital accessibility. The meeting included representatives from the Ministry of External Affairs and various national technical divisions as part of a scheduled visit to India.

stories.title: Design exhibition to showcase student talent in Nagpur
stories.summary: Bhanwar Rathore Design Studio is hosting a design exhibition in Nagpur on November 22, 2026. The event features creative work from students across fashion, architecture, and graphic design. The exhibition is part of an annual initiative conducted across 15 major Indian cities to promote design education.

LDHS senior wins STEAM logo contest
stories.summary: Noah Smith, a senior at Laurens District 55 High School, won the district's STEAM on the Square logo design contest. The award was presented by the interim superintendent and the director of teaching and learning at a school board meeting. The student is a digital art specialist.

stories.title: Vadnagar Museum wins Red Dot award
stories.summary: The Anant Anadi Vadnagar Archaeological Experiential Museum has received the Red Dot Best of the Best Award 2026. The museum features recovered artefacts and an excavation site connected by a bridge. It is the first and only museum in India to receive this specific distinction.

stories.title: Levista Coffee refreshes brand identity
stories.summary: Levista Coffee has unveiled a new brand identity and campaign titled Taste the Joy of Coorg. The company aims to associate its instant, filter, and cold coffee products with the natural beauty and cultural heritage of the Coorg region. The brand is part of the SLN Group.

stories.title: Levista Coffee refreshes brand identity with new logo and campaign
stories.summary: Levista Coffee, the coffee brand from SLN Group, has introduced a refreshed brand identity and packaging as part of a rebranding exercise centred on its origins in Coorg. The change is accompanied by a new campaign, ‘Taste the Joy of Coorg’, which links the brand's identity to the region's coffee

Boltz raises $110 million for AI drug design
stories.summary: Boltz has raised $110 million in Series A funding to develop AI models for pharmaceutical researchers. The company reports a 50-fold increase in paid usage since June. The models provide early clues for researchers, though the company notes they are not finished medicines.

stories.summary: Bessemer-led Series A will fund headcount and computing infrastructure for Boltz's molecule and protein design models. stories.title: Vaxdigm secures government R&D funding
stories.summary: Vaxdigm has been selected for a Ministry of Health and Welfare project to develop a generative AI-based vaccine design platform. The company received 600 million KRW in government funding and plans to integrate its proprietary protein expression technology. It recently hired three AI specialists.

stories.title: Q-CTRL raises $290 million in Series C
stories.summary: Sydney-based quantum software company Q-CTRL has raised 290 million USD in a Series C round led by Salesforce Ventures. The round was oversubscribed and included participation from AMD Ventures and Lockheed Martin Ventures. The company is one of five Australian startups to announce funding this week.

stories.title: Anthropic raises $81.3 billion in IPO
stories.summary: Anthropic has raised 81.3 billion USD in its Nasdaq debut, valuing the company at 1.5 trillion USD. The offering surpasses the 75 billion USD raised by SpaceX. The company reports rapid revenue growth alongside widening losses as it tests investor appetite for artificial intelligence.

stories.title: Urban Company raises 2,500 crore via QIP
stories.summary: Urban Company has raised 2,500 crore through a qualified institutional placement. The company received bids worth 15,000 crore, six times the size of the issue. Proceeds are intended for brand marketing and the supply ecosystem for its on-demand household help services.

stories.title: Urban Company Raises ₹2,500 Cr Via QIP, Draws Bids Worth Over ₹15,000 Cr
stories.summary: Home services marketplace Urban Company has raised ₹2,500 Cr through a qualified institutional placement (QIP), attracting bids worth over ₹15,000 Cr, more than 6X the issue size. The issue opened on November 16 (Monday) and closed yesterday. More than 60 investors submitted bids, with shares allocated to 33 investors. Of

stories.title: Consumer durables market projected to grow
stories.summary: A report by BCG and the CII projects India's consumer durables market will reach 3 lakh to 3.25 lakh crore by 2030. Growth is expected to be driven by rising household incomes and financing access. A significant portion of the market opportunity may still be met by imports.

stories.title: Creatives face job displacement from AI
stories.summary: As AI tools become cheaper and more capable, creative professionals report job losses and displacement. Voice actor Matti Klemm is currently taking legal action against Netflix, alleging his voice was used to train AI without permission. The industry continues to debate the role of human labor.

stories.title: Bloomberg analysis shows AI-exposed roles in China falling faster
stories.summary: Bloomberg analysis of 10 million job postings suggests AI is putting additional pressure on China's labor market. Listings for roles highly exposed to AI fell 10 percentage points more than those for less affected positions between July 2021 and June 2025. The economy is struggling to keep pace.

stories.title: Studio jobs roundup lists 78 openings
stories.summary: The latest AWN Jobs Roundup features 78 new listings from studios including Crunchyroll, Electronic Arts, and Netflix. Roles range from engineering and data to VFX and animation, with locations spanning Montreal, London, and Shanghai. The industry continues to post openings for those who have not yet been replaced.

stories.title: Canva cuts 1,271 jobs in refounding overhaul
stories.summary: Canva is eliminating 1,271 positions, or 22 percent of its global workforce, as the company restructures to return to a small-team model. CEO Melanie Perkins described the move as an effort to refound the firm. Growth at the company slowed this year for the first time in a decade.

stories.title: Bryan Johnson longevity habits on a budget
stories.summary: Tech entrepreneur Bryan Johnson is known for his intensive Blueprint health programme involving medical testing and specialised treatments. While his full approach requires significant capital, some of his recommendations focus on everyday habits like sleep and exercise. Longevity is now available to those without a private medical team.

stories.title: Data visualization illustrates billionaire wealth
stories.summary: A new data story contrasts the median US household income of $59,228 with the earnings of the world's richest individuals. The analysis notes that Elon Musk earns the equivalent of a typical annual salary in 23 seconds. The scale of wealth remains difficult to visualize for most.

Amazon Prime India head Abhinav Agarwal departs
stories.summary: Abhinav Agarwal has left his role as director and head of Amazon Prime India after 16 years with the company. He led the product, marketing, and engineering teams responsible for growing the programme in Bengaluru. He stated his next role will involve commerce, logistics, and product.

stories.title: Rebranding as an act of calculated amnesia
stories.summary: Brands often change their identity to remain relevant in a competitive market. This process requires companies to discard the recognition that previously made them valuable. The strategy relies on the hope that customers will forget what came before.

stories.title: Bangkok International Design Expo opens next week
stories.summary: The World Ends design expo arrives at Bangkok Kunsthalle on November 25. Organized by the Thailand Convention and Exhibition Bureau, the event features workshops and talks under the theme Create What Matters. The organizers claim the name refers to the end of old ways of doing things.

research.title: A Human-Centric Adaptive Multi-Fidelity Digital Twin Framework for Cyber-Physical Systems
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Digital twins of cyber-physical systems must operate with scarce data, on assets that change after deployment, and for humans whose needs differ, yet existing implementations fix fidelity at design time and do not match the representation. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: AI Deactivation Reduces Loneliness and Increases Social Interaction
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: General-purpose artificial intelligence (AI) assistants are increasingly embedded in everyday life, transforming how people accomplish tasks and potentially reshaping how they interact with others. Prior research has focused on how using AI for explicitly social purposes. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: AI-Induced Social Erosion: Using LLMs for Work Tasks Reduces Help-Seeking Intentions Towards Colleagues
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative AI is becoming embedded in knowledge work as an intelligent collaborator to assist in completing tasks. However, this readily available assistance risks displacing key interactions through which colleague relationships are built and sustained at work. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: CoMPASS: A Multi-Turn Benchmark for Measuring LLM Reinforcement of Parasocial Behavior
research.summary: Announce Type: cross Abstract: Users of conversational LLMs sometimes anthropomorphize these systems, form emotional attachments to them, and become dependent on them. This behavior, known as parasocial attachment, has been linked to multiple documented fatalities. However, public benchmarks for measuring. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Crisis Governance at the Joints. Mapping the Ethical and Societal Territory of Crisis Management Technologies: The Case of Human-Swarm Teami
research.summary: Announce Type: cross Abstract: Crisis and disaster governance increasingly relies on technologies that sense, classify and act faster than humans can. Drone swarms coordinated with human operators, known as human-swarm teaming, provide a productive case to review the field of. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Design and Evaluation of Epira: An Automated Interview System for Case Investigation and Contact Tracing
research.summary: Announce Type: cross Abstract: Objective: Case investigation and contact tracing are labor-intensive. Web forms struggle when respondents need clarification before disclosing contacts, and open-ended chatbots may deviate from protocols. We developed and evaluated Epira, a protocol-controlled large language model (LLM). Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Design and Evaluation of a Body-Machine Interface as an Alternative Control Paradigm for Pedal-based Sewing Machines
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Body-machine interfaces (BoMIs) exploit body movements to control assistive devices, they have been evaluated primarily in tasks such as cursor control or robotic manipulation where the entire movement repertoire is devoted toward device control. However, tasks. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Designing Algorithmic Recommendations to Achieve Human-AI Complementarity
research.summary: Announce Type: replace Abstract: Algorithms frequently assist, rather than replace, human decision-makers. However, the design and analysis of algorithms often focus on predicting outcomes and do not explicitly model their effect on human decisions. This discrepancy between the design and. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
